title: EXercise-induced PhysioLogical Adaptations In Neurological Disorders
summary:
The goal of this study is to investigate how a one-time exercise session influences different parameters of brain function in people with neurological diseases compared to healthy volunteers. The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* How do fitness level, exercise performance, and physical exhaustion differ between patients with neurological diseases and healthy participants?
* How does acute exercise affect brain function and other physiological biomarkers in participants with neurological diseases?

Participants will take part in a single, one-day study visit and will be asked to:

* Perform a standardized exercise test on a bicycle ergometer
* Undergo a brain MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) scan, a blood draw, and autonomic measurements before and after the exercise test
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18 years or older
* Clinical diagnosis of one of the following neurological diseases: epilepsy, functional neurological disorder, mild cognitive impairment, dementia, Parkinson's disease, concussion, brain tumor \[for participants with neurological diseases\]
* No diagnosis of neurological disease \[for healthy control participants\]

Exclusion Criteria:

* Non-english speaking individuals
* Exercise contraindications (e.g., physical impairments limiting use of bicycle ergometer, acute infections, severe heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension, exercise associated seizures)
* Current use of medications for cardiac rhythm or rate control
* Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contraindications (e.g., electrical implants, ferromagnetic implants or objects, pregnancy)
